walkthroughs.body_html:
Problem Solving With Programming — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Problem Solving With Programming brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Problem Solving With Programming.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which is a high-level programming language?
options: Assembly
Machine code
Python
Binary
Internet Data Engine
Integrated Development Environment
Internal Debugging Editor
Interpreted Dynamic Executable

mcqs.q: What does it mean that RAM is volatile?
options: Its contents are lost when power is removed.
Any item, randomly.
It can store data permanently.
It can explode or be damaged easily.

mcqs.q: Which item is removed first from a stack?
options: The first one added (FIFO).
Any item, randomly.
They produce different programming languages.
The most recently added (top) - LIFO.

mcqs.q: What is the key difference between a compiler and an interpreter?
options: It can store data permanently.
A compiler is a person, an interpreter is software.
A compiler translates the whole program first; an interpreter executes line by line.
They produce different programming languages.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Comment”?
options: Programming language close to human language (Python, Java) that must be translated to machine code.
Non-executing text in source code that explains the program to human readers.
Meaning of a syntactically valid program - what the code actually does when executed.
Assembly or machine code, closer to hardware, providing direct control of the processor.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Low-level language”?
options: Set of rules defining valid combinations of symbols and keywords in a programming language.
Assembly or machine code, closer to hardware, providing direct control of the processor.
Integrated Development Environment: editor, compiler/interpreter, debugger and tools combined in one application.
Non-executing text in source code that explains the program to human readers.
